title: Plurai wants to help AI agents work better using the same approach that helped get self-driving cars to roads
slides: Why do AI agents still fail at real work?
Plurai borrows a method from self-driving car development
It simulates agent environments instead of real-world testing
Teams can now stress-test agents before deployment
Ask your agent vendor what simulation they ran
thread_text:
1. AI agents fail at real work

Self-driving car teams learned that simulation beats road testing. Now that method is coming to AI agents, and most vendors haven't told you if they use it.

2. Borrowing from self-driving cars

Plurai adapts the same simulation-first approach used to train autonomous vehicles. Instead of deploying agents into production to learn from failures, they build synthetic environments first.

3. Simulate before deployment

Teams can now stress-test AI agents against thousands of simulated scenarios before they ever touch real users. Failures happen in the simulator, not in your workflow.

4. The question vendors fear

Ask your AI agent provider what simulation they ran. If they can't answer, you're the test environment. That's a risk you're paying for.

5. Test your agent this week

Take one task your agent handles and ask the vendor for their simulation results. No simulation means no evidence. Start there before you deploy again.
